lessonTitle: KT 1.0: Broken Promises & Imperial Borders: Why Was Conflict in the Middle East Inevitable?
title: Imperial War Museums: Britain's WWI Gamble & The Origins of the Conflict
teacher_guidance: Examines how Britain made contradictory wartime promises to Arab leaders (McMahon-Hussein Correspondence) and Zionists (Balfour Declaration) to secure imperial dominance in the Middle East. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–04:30 • Lesson Phase: Starter Hook (0–5m). Tone Alert: Authoritative archival analysis from the Imperial War Museums; objectively presents how imperial strategic priorities outweighed regional self-determination.
viewing_task:
1. [01:10] Recall: Which three diplomatic agreements did the British government negotiate between 1915 and 1917 regarding the future governance of Ottoman territories?
  2. [02:45] Explain: Explain why the British War Cabinet decided that issuing the Balfour Declaration in November 1917 was essential to Britain's global imperial strategy during the First World War.
  3. [04:00] Challenge: Analyze the contradictory nature of British wartime pledges. To what extent did British imperial diplomacy deliberately sow the seeds of intractable conflict between Arab and Jewish populations?

lessonTitle: KT 1.0: Broken Promises & Imperial Borders: Why Was Conflict in the Middle East Inevitable?
title: The Economist: The Balfour Declaration's Impact, 100 Years On
teacher_guidance: Rigorous journalistic analysis of the 67-word Balfour Declaration, contrasting Jewish national aspirations with Palestinian Arab dispossession. Recommended Watch Window: 01:20–05:50 • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Dual-Coding. Tone Alert: Analytical modern geopolitical journalism; provides clear visual text deconstruction of the original 67-word letter.
viewing_task:
1. [01:45] Recall: How many words were contained in the original Balfour Declaration letter addressed to Lord Rothschild in November 1917?
  2. [03:20] Explain: Explain how the deliberate ambiguity of the phrase 'national home for the Jewish people'—and the omission of political rights for the Arab majority—created conflicting legal expectations.
  3. [05:10] Challenge: Evaluate the second clause of the Declaration: 'nothing shall be done which may prejudice the civil and religious rights of existing non-Jewish communities'. Why do Arab historians consider this phrasing deeply patronizing and legally hollow?

lessonTitle: KT 1.0: Broken Promises & Imperial Borders: Why Was Conflict in the Middle East Inevitable?
title: Imperial War Museums: Mandatory Palestine, The 1936 Arab Revolt & The 1939 White Paper
teacher_guidance: Investigates the breakdown of British Mandate governance during the 1930s, escalating Jewish immigration fleeing European Nazism, the general strike of 1936, and the 1939 White Paper immigration caps. Recommended Watch Window: 02:00–07:15 • Lesson Phase: Source Analysis & Evidence. Tone Alert: Archival footage and primary colonial records illustrating the brutal counter-insurgency tactics employed by British troops during the 1936–39 revolt.
viewing_task:
1. [02:40] Recall: What economic action did the Arab Higher Committee launch in April 1936 to protest against surging Jewish immigration and British colonial policy?
  2. [04:30] Explain: Explain how the threat of imminent war against Nazi Germany in Europe forced the British government to reverse its Zionist policy by issuing the May 1939 White Paper.
  3. [06:45] Challenge: Analyze the tragic timing and moral consequences of the 1939 White Paper. Why did David Ben-Gurion state: 'We will fight the White Paper as if there is no war, and fight the war as if there is no White Paper'?

lessonTitle: KT 1.0: Broken Promises & Imperial Borders: Why Was Conflict in the Middle East Inevitable?
title: BBC / ERA: Israel and the Arab States – The Collapse of the Mandate
teacher_guidance: Authoritative BBC archive documentary covering the League of Nations Mandate, escalating communal violence, and Britain's postwar decision to abandon Palestine. Recommended Watch Window: 08:30–14:45 • Lesson Phase: High-Attainer Stretch & Oral History Investigation. Tone Alert: Classic BBC documentary featuring veteran British soldiers, Haganah underground fighters, and Palestinian elders reflecting on the tragic collapse of order in 1945–1947.
viewing_task:
1. [09:15] Recall: Which three underground Zionist paramilitary organizations launched insurgent attacks against British forces between 1945 and 1947?
  2. [11:40] Explain: Explain why post-war Britain, bankrupt from fighting World War II and under intense international pressure, found Mandatory Palestine ungovernable by 1947.
  3. [13:50] Challenge: Evaluate how oral testimonies from both British colonial administrators and Jewish and Arab veterans illustrate the total breakdown of British authority. Why did Britain choose to refer Palestine to the UN rather than implement partition themselves?

lessonTitle: KT 1.1: The End of the British Mandate and the Creation of Israel, 1945–1949
title: British Pathé: King David Hotel Bombing Newsreel (July 1946)
teacher_guidance: Contemporary British newsreel recording the devastation of the British military headquarters in Jerusalem. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–03:16 (Full Newsreel) • Lesson Phase: Starter Hook (0–5m). Tone Alert: Produced for British domestic cinema audiences in 1946; employs emotive wartime rhetoric ('dastardly crime', 'gang of desperados') and Blitz comparisons to rally public sympathy for British soldiers.
viewing_task:
1. [00:45] Recall: Which wing of the King David Hotel was destroyed, and what two British administrative bodies were headquartered there?
  2. [01:50] Explain: Explain why the bombing of the King David Hotel by Menachem Begin's Irgun convinced British ministers that maintaining peacekeeping forces in Mandatory Palestine was politically untenable.
  3. [02:30] Challenge: Analyze the newsreel narrator's choice of language and dramatic framing. How does comparing the wreckage to 'the Blitz' shape British public perceptions of Zionist insurgents and justify British withdrawal?

lessonTitle: KT 1.1: The End of the British Mandate and the Creation of Israel, 1945–1949
title: Unpacked (Avi Posen): Resolution 181 – The Zionist Dream & Acceptance of Partition
teacher_guidance: Avi Posen examines the 29 November 1947 UN vote partitioning Palestine. Recommended Watch Window: 01:45–06:20 (4m 35s) • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Dual-Coding. Tone Alert: Engaging mainstream Israeli educational framing. Notice how Posen balances Jewish post-Holocaust relief with the painful concession of internationalising Jerusalem, while using conversational American framing ('US-backed arm-twisting').
viewing_task:
1. [02:15] Recall: In 1937, what percentage of land did the Peel Commission propose allocating to the Arab and Jewish populations?
  2. [03:40] Explain: Explain why David Ben-Gurion and the Jewish Agency accepted UN Resolution 181 despite being allocated non-contiguous territory and losing direct sovereign control over Jerusalem.
  3. [05:10] Challenge: Analyze how the presenter explains the Palestinian Arab rejection of partition. Does the video provide sufficient historical empathy for Arab demographic grievances regarding land ownership?

lessonTitle: KT 1.1: The End of the British Mandate and the Creation of Israel, 1945–1949
title: Janux: Palestine Population & Jewish Immigration (1880–1948)
teacher_guidance: Academic demographic lecture illustrating the statistical foundations of the 1947 conflict. Recommended Watch Window: 01:10–05:40 (4m 30s) • Lesson Phase: Source Analysis & Comparative Homework. Tone Alert: Rigorous, dispassionate academic demographic analysis grounded in 1922 and 1931 British colonial censuses and 1947 UNSCOP land records. Essential for countering the historical misconception of an 'empty land'.
viewing_task:
1. [01:30] Recall: What proportion of Mandatory Palestine's total population was Palestinian Arab in 1947, according to British census records?
  2. [03:15] Explain: Explain why Palestinian Arab leaders argued that UN Resolution 181 was inherently undemocratic, particularly regarding the allocation of 55% of the land to the Jewish minority.
  3. [04:45] Challenge: Compare this demographic lecture with political speeches of 1947. Why is statistical land registration crucial evidence when evaluating conflicting historical claims to the justice of partition?

lessonTitle: KT 1.1: The End of the British Mandate and the Creation of Israel, 1945–1949
title: Otto Preminger's "Exodus" (1960) Theatrical Trailer starring Paul Newman
teacher_guidance: Hollywood epic dramatization starring Paul Newman based on Leon Uris's bestseller. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–02:48 (Full Trailer) • Lesson Phase: Cultural & Media Deconstruction. Tone Alert: High-impact 1960 American cinema. Depicts Haganah freedom fighters as glamorous underdogs against British naval tyranny, completely omitting indigenous Palestinian Arab society from the founding narrative.
viewing_task:
1. [00:30] Recall: What was the name of the refugee ship depicted in the trailer, and what nationality was the naval force blockading the coast of Palestine?
  2. [01:15] Explain: Explain how the real-world international media coverage of the SS Exodus in July 1947 damaged Britain's diplomatic standing and undermined its moral authority in the United States.
  3. [02:00] Challenge: Analyze the music, dramatic narration, and casting of Paul Newman in this 1960 trailer. How does Hollywood cinematic storytelling construct a mythologized founding narrative, and whose historical presence is erased?

lessonTitle: KT 1.1: The End of the British Mandate and the Creation of Israel, 1945–1949
title: BBC / PBS: The 50 Years War – Land Divided (1947–1956)
teacher_guidance: Definitive oral history documentary featuring on-camera interviews with Israeli veterans, Arab commanders, and British diplomats. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–10:15 (10m 15s) • Lesson Phase: High-Attainer Stretch & Oral History Investigation. Tone Alert: Award-winning dual-perspective oral testimony; provides unmatched classroom insight into the confusion, fears, and strategic calculations of May 1948.
viewing_task:
1. [02:40] Recall: On what date and in what city did David Ben-Gurion proclaim the establishment of the State of Israel?
  2. [05:30] Explain: Explain how Britain's abrupt, uncoordinated withdrawal on 14 May 1948 transformed a localized civil conflict between communal militias into a full-scale regional interstate war.
  3. [08:15] Challenge: Evaluate the oral testimony of British and Arab veterans in this documentary. How do their retrospective accounts decades later challenge simplistic textbook summaries of the outbreak of the 1948 War?

lessonTitle: KT 1.2: The Aftermath of the 1948–49 War & The Palestinian Refugee Crisis
title: ForCriticalThinkers: 1948 – War of Independence or Al-Nakba?
teacher_guidance: Essential conceptual starter comparing the diametrically opposed historical memories of 1948: miraculous national rebirth vs catastrophic displacement. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–04:45 • Lesson Phase: Starter Hook (0–5m). Tone Alert: Thoughtful historiographical comparison illustrating how the same military events in 1948 produced two completely irreconcilable national historical narratives.
viewing_task:
1. [01:10] Recall: What Arabic word is used by Palestinians to describe the 1948 catastrophe, and what Hebrew term is used by Israelis?
  2. [02:40] Explain: Explain why the 1948 war is interpreted simultaneously as an existential miracle of survival by Israelis and a catastrophe of dispossession by Palestinians.
  3. [04:15] Challenge: Analyze the concept of dual historical memory. How do these conflicting 1948 narratives continue to prevent diplomatic reconciliation over the 'Right of Return' today?

lessonTitle: KT 1.2: The Aftermath of the 1948–49 War & The Palestinian Refugee Crisis
title: Unpacked (Avi Posen): 1948 Israeli War of Independence & Defence of Statehood
teacher_guidance: Avi Posen examines the military balance in 1948, the initial Arab advances, Haganah reorganization into the IDF, and the acquisition of Czechoslovak weapons during the first UN truce. Recommended Watch Window: 01:30–06:45 • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Dual-Coding. Tone Alert: Mainstream Israeli educational framing; emphasizes high combat motivation and unified command while explaining the pivotal significance of the Czechoslovak arms airlift.
viewing_task:
1. [02:00] Recall: Which European country supplied Israel with vital rifles, machine guns, and fighter aircraft during the first UN truce in June 1948?
  2. [03:50] Explain: Explain how unified military command under David Ben-Gurion and the dissolution of paramilitaries into the IDF gave Israel a decisive tactical advantage over divided Arab armies.
  3. [05:30] Challenge: Evaluate the presenter's discussion of Arab army strength in 1948. How do modern 'New Historians' (such as Avi Shlaim) challenge the traditional narrative that tiny Israel faced overwhelmingly superior Arab numbers?

lessonTitle: KT 1.2: The Aftermath of the 1948–49 War & The Palestinian Refugee Crisis
title: Al Jazeera English: How Did the Nakba Happen? The 1948 Refugee Crisis
teacher_guidance: Examines the expulsion and flight of 700,000+ Palestinian Arabs, the controversy surrounding Plan Dalet, the Deir Yassin massacre, and the creation of UNRWA refugee camps. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–05:15 • Lesson Phase: Source Analysis & Evidence. Tone Alert: Emotive Palestinian historical perspective utilizing archival maps, village survivor testimonies, and British colonial reports documenting forced displacement.
viewing_task:
1. [01:15] Recall: How many Palestinian Arab villages were depopulated or destroyed during the 1948 war, according to historical documentation?
  2. [02:50] Explain: Explain how events like the Deir Yassin massacre in April 1948 and military operations under Plan Dalet caused widespread civilian panic and flight.
  3. [04:40] Challenge: Analyze the historiographical debate between traditional Israeli historians (who argued Arabs left voluntarily on orders from Arab radio broadcasts) and New Historians (such as Benny Morris). What do archival records reveal?

lessonTitle: KT 1.2: The Aftermath of the 1948–49 War & The Palestinian Refugee Crisis
title: TRT World: The 1949 Armistice Agreements & The Reshaped Borders
teacher_guidance: Examines the Green Line armistice borders agreed in Rhodes in 1949, Israel's territorial expansion to 78% of the mandate, and the division of Jerusalem. Recommended Watch Window: 00:30–04:45 • Lesson Phase: High-Attainer Stretch & Cartographic Analysis. Tone Alert: Clear cartographic animation tracing how the armistices permanently erased the proposed Palestinian Arab state and partitioned Jerusalem.
viewing_task:
1. [01:05] Recall: What island hosted the 1949 UN-brokered armistice talks between Israel and neighboring Arab states, and what color ink was used to draw the boundary lines?
  2. [02:30] Explain: Explain how the 1949 Armistice Agreements altered the territorial division of Palestine compared to the 1947 UN Partition Plan (Resolution 181).
  3. [04:10] Challenge: Why did the 1949 Armistice Agreements intentionally avoid establishing permanent international borders, and how did this ambiguity ensure continued regional conflict?

lessonTitle: KT 1.3: Increased Tension, Nasser, and the Suez Crisis, 1955–1963
title: The History Channel: Why the 1956 Suez Crisis Brought the World to the Brink
teacher_guidance: Fast-paced overview of Gamal Abdel Nasser, the Egyptian nationalisation of the Suez Canal Company on 26 July 1956, and the Anglo-French crisis. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–03:45 (Full Clip) • Lesson Phase: Starter Hook (0–5m). Tone Alert: Fast-paced historical summary highlighting Cold War tensions and imperial desperation.
viewing_task:
1. [00:45] Recall: In which Egyptian city and on what date did President Gamal Abdel Nasser publicly announce the nationalisation of the Suez Canal?
  2. [01:50] Explain: Explain why British Prime Minister Anthony Eden viewed Nasser's nationalisation not merely as a commercial dispute, but as an existential threat to British imperial prestige and Middle Eastern oil supplies.
  3. [02:40] Challenge: Analyze how Eden's personal experience of 1930s European appeasement led him to fatally misjudge President Nasser as an 'Egyptian Hitler' who had to be overthrown.

lessonTitle: KT 1.3: Increased Tension, Nasser, and the Suez Crisis, 1955–1963
title: Epic History TV: The Brink of War – The Suez Crisis (Part 1)
teacher_guidance: Detailed cartographic breakdown of the secret Sèvres Agreement collusion between Britain, France, and Israel to stage an Israeli attack on Sinai to justify Anglo-French intervention. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–07:30 • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Dual-Coding. Tone Alert: Objective military-cartographic animation; reveals the clandestine diplomatic deception that destroyed British international moral standing.
viewing_task:
1. [02:15] Recall: In which private villa outside Paris did British, French, and Israeli delegations sign the secret Sèvres Agreement in October 1956?
  2. [04:20] Explain: What three-part military timetable did the conspirators arrange at Sèvres to provide Britain and France with a pretext to seize the Suez Canal?
  3. [06:10] Challenge: Analyze the strategic motives of Israel: why was Prime Minister David Ben-Gurion willing to collude with colonial powers Britain and France to invade the Sinai Peninsula?

lessonTitle: KT 1.3: Increased Tension, Nasser, and the Suez Crisis, 1955–1963
title: Epic History TV: A Global Flashpoint – The Suez Crisis (Part 2)
teacher_guidance: Examines President Eisenhower's financial ultimatum threatening to crash the British pound, Soviet nuclear threats, and the permanent decline of European imperial power. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–06:30 • Lesson Phase: Source Analysis & Evidence. Tone Alert: Detailed geopolitical analysis exploring superpower diplomacy and financial coercion.
viewing_task:
1. [01:30] Recall: Which US President issued the economic ultimatum to Britain, and what global financial institution did the US block from assisting London?
  2. [03:45] Explain: Explain why the United States adamantly opposed the Anglo-French invasion of Egypt, despite Britain being America's closest NATO ally.
  3. [05:20] Challenge: Evaluate why historians consider the 1956 Suez Crisis the defining event that ended Britain and France's status as independent global superpowers.

teacher_guidance: In-depth documentary exploring Nasser's domestic reforms, radio diplomacy (Voice of the Arabs), and the anti-imperialist mobilization of the Arab world. Tone Alert: Rich French-Arab documentary featuring primary radio recordings and public rallies celebrating anti-colonial defiance.
viewing_task:
1. [06:15] Recall: What Cairo-based radio broadcasting station did President Nasser use to beam fiery anti-colonial speeches into homes and coffee houses across the Middle East?
  2. [08:50] Explain: How did President Nasser turn a total tactical military defeat in the Sinai desert into a magnificent political and diplomatic triumph across the Arab world?
  3. [11:15] Challenge: Analyze the long-term impact of Nasser's Pan-Arab charisma. How did the Suez victory elevate expectations among Arab populations that proved dangerously unsustainable by 1967?

lessonTitle: KT 2.1 Enquiry: How Did Water, Border Raids, and Rhetoric Make a Second Arab-Israeli War Inevitable? (1964–1967)
title: Historical Archive: Who Will Fire First? The May 1967 Brinkmanship
teacher_guidance: Dramatic breakdown of the rapid diplomatic unraveling in May 1967: Soviet false intelligence, Nasser massing 100,000 troops in Sinai, expelling UNEF, and blockading the Straits of Tiran. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–05:15 • Lesson Phase: Starter Hook (0–5m). Tone Alert: Dramatic archival newsreel footage capturing the sudden plunge from uneasy peace into existential regional crisis.
viewing_task:
1. [01:10] Recall: What international peacekeeping force did President Nasser order to immediately evacuate the Sinai border on 16 May 1967?
  2. [02:40] Explain: Why did the State of Israel consider President Nasser's closure of the Straits of Tiran to Israeli shipping on 22 May 1967 an explicit act of war (casus belli)?
  3. [04:20] Challenge: Evaluate the role of political brinkmanship: did President Nasser genuinely intend to launch an unprovoked invasion of Israel, or did he become a prisoner of his own public rhetoric and regional Arab rivalry?

lessonTitle: KT 2.1 Enquiry: How Did Water, Border Raids, and Rhetoric Make a Second Arab-Israeli War Inevitable? (1964–1967)
title: Historical Documentary: The War Over Water & Syrian Border Clashes (1964–1966)
teacher_guidance: Explores the Jordan River diversion disputes, Israeli air and artillery strikes on Syrian earthmoving machinery, and the escalation of cross-border skirmishes on the Golan Heights. Recommended Watch Window: 00:45–05:30 • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Dual-Coding. Tone Alert: Rigorous geographical and military analysis of ecological resource competition as a primary causal driver.
viewing_task:
1. [01:30] Recall: What major engineering project did Israel complete in 1964 to pump water to the arid Negev desert, and what counter-scheme was launched by the Arab League?
  2. [03:15] Explain: Explain how Syrian military positions on the high cliffs of the Golan Heights held a commanding tactical advantage over Israeli agricultural kibbutzim in the Hula Valley below.
  3. [04:50] Challenge: To what extent was the outbreak of the Six-Day War driven by competition over vital ecological resources (freshwater) rather than purely ideological or religious hostility?

lessonTitle: KT 2.1 Enquiry: How Did Water, Border Raids, and Rhetoric Make a Second Arab-Israeli War Inevitable? (1964–1967)
title: Gulf News / Archival: May 1967: Nasser, Arab Alliances & Soviet Warnings

Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–03:22 (Full Clip) • Lesson Phase: Source Analysis & Evidence. viewing_task:
1. [00:50] Recall: Which global superpower delivered fabricated intelligence reports to Egyptian officials on 13 May 1967 falsely claiming Israel was massing twelve brigades on the Syrian border?
  2. [01:45] Explain: Why was King Hussein of Jordan compelled to fly to Cairo on 30 May 1967 to sign a mutual defense pact with his bitter ideological rival, President Nasser?
  3. [02:40] Challenge: Analyze the explosive impact of Arab radio propaganda and mass street demonstrations in May 1967. How did public passion limit the ability of Arab leaders to pursue diplomatic compromise?

lessonTitle: KT 2.1 Enquiry: How Did Water, Border Raids, and Rhetoric Make a Second Arab-Israeli War Inevitable? (1964–1967)
title: BBC / ERA: Days That Shook the World – The Six-Day War (Part 1)

Tone Alert: Immersive BBC dramatized documentary with firsthand Israeli cabinet and military testimonies.
viewing_task:
1. [03:40] Recall: What Hebrew term was given to the agonizing three-week period of national dread, diplomatic paralysis, and military waiting in Israel between 16 May and 5 June 1967?
  2. [06:15] Explain: Why did the Israeli coalition cabinet under Prime Minister Levi Eshkol and newly appointed Defence Minister Moshe Dayan conclude that pre-emptive offensive action was necessary for national survival?
  3. [09:50] Challenge: Contrast the intense public terror among Israeli civilians (who dug 10,000 mass graves in public parks in Tel Aviv) with the meticulous operational confidence of Israeli Air Force commanders.

lessonTitle: KT 2.2 Enquiry: Why Was the Six-Day War Decided in Three Hours, and Did Nasser Intend to Fight? (May–June 1967)

viewing_task:
1. [01:05] Recall: What was the military codename of the surprise Israeli pre-emptive air strike launched at 07:45 on the morning of 5 June 1967?
  2. [02:30] Explain: Explain how the destruction of over 300 Egyptian combat aircraft on the ground in the first three hours decided the entire outcome of the Six-Day War.
  3. [03:50] Challenge: By 10 June 1967, Israel had captured territories three times its original size. How did this astonishing victory transform Israel from a vulnerable state into an occupying power with complex demographic problems?

lessonTitle: KT 2.2 Enquiry: Why Was the Six-Day War Decided in Three Hours, and Did Nasser Intend to Fight? (May–June 1967)

viewing_task:

  3. [07:15] Challenge: Analyze the factors behind Israeli military dominance: how did superior pilot training, ground turnaround speed (jets refueled and rearmed in under 8 minutes), and decentralized officer initiative explain Israel's victory over numerically larger Arab armies?

lessonTitle: KT 2.2 Enquiry: Why Was the Six-Day War Decided in Three Hours, and Did Nasser Intend to Fight? (May–June 1967)

viewing_task:

  2. [04:15] Explain: Why did the capture of the Old City and the Western Wall evoke such an extraordinary outpouring of tears and euphoria across the Jewish world?
  3. [05:50] Challenge: Deconstruct the term 'reunification of Jerusalem'. How do Palestinians and international bodies view the annexation of East Jerusalem under international law, and why does this remain one of the most explosive issues in the world?

lessonTitle: KT 2.2 Enquiry: Why Was the Six-Day War Decided in Three Hours, and Did Nasser Intend to Fight? (May–June 1967)

  3. [18:30] Challenge: Evaluate oral testimonies from both Jordanian legionnaires and Israeli paratroopers. How do their personal memories challenge simplistic one-sided narratives of cowardice or effortless victory?

  3. [03:50] Challenge: Analyze the crucial linguistic loophole between the English version ('withdrawal from territories occupied') and the French version ('retrait des territoires occupés'). Why did this linguistic ambiguity cause decades of diplomatic stalemate?

lessonTitle: KT 2.3 Enquiry: "Land for Peace" or Permanent Stalemate: How Did the 1967 Conquered Territories Transform the Conflict?

  3. [03:10] Challenge: How did the Khartoum Resolution's 'Three Noes' reinforce Israeli domestic arguments that the captured territories should not be returned, cementing the diplomatic stalemate?

lessonTitle: KT 2.3 Enquiry: "Land for Peace" or Permanent Stalemate: How Did the 1967 Conquered Territories Transform the Conflict?

  3. [05:10] Challenge: Evaluate how the construction of settlements, bypass roads, and military zones established 'irreversible facts on the ground', making a viable, contiguous two-state solution extraordinarily difficult to implement.

lessonTitle: KT 2.3 Enquiry: "Land for Peace" or Permanent Stalemate: How Did the 1967 Conquered Territories Transform the Conflict?

  2. [36:20] Explain: What was the profound 'demographic dilemma' that Israeli leaders confronted regarding whether to formally annex the newly captured territories?
  3. [39:45] Challenge: Analyze the debate between Moshe Dayan (who believed Israel could manage an 'invisible occupation' through economic integration) and Foreign Minister Abba Eban (who warned that ruling over a hostile million-strong population would rot Israeli democracy).

lessonTitle: KT 2.4: The Rise of Palestinian Resistance: The PLO, Black September & Munich (1968–1972)

  2. [03:10] Explain: Why did the Black September militant faction choose the Munich Olympic Games—billed as the 'Peace Olympics'—to launch their hostage-taking operation?
  3. [04:45] Challenge: How did the botched rescue attempt by unprepared Bavarian police at Fürstenfeldbruck airfield expose the total lack of modern counter-terrorism capabilities in Western democracies?

lessonTitle: KT 2.4: The Rise of Palestinian Resistance: The PLO, Black September & Munich (1968–1972)

  3. [06:20] Challenge: Analyze the regional consequences of Jordan's military crackdown: where did Yasser Arafat and the PLO relocate their armed headquarters, and how did this destabilize Lebanon?

lessonTitle: KT 2.4: The Rise of Palestinian Resistance: The PLO, Black September & Munich (1968–1972)

lessonTitle: KT 2.4: The Rise of Palestinian Resistance: The PLO, Black September & Munich (1968–1972)

lessonTitle: KT 2.4: The Rise of Palestinian Resistance: The PLO, Black September & Munich (1968–1972)

lessonTitle: KT 2.4: The Rise of Palestinian Resistance: The PLO, Black September & Munich (1968–1972)

  3. [05:40] Challenge: Analyze the epic tank battle in the 'Valley of Tears' on the Golan Heights: why was the Centurion stand by the outnumbered Israeli 7th Armored Brigade crucial to preventing Syria from capturing northern Israel?

  3. [05:15] Challenge: How did the Arab OPEC oil embargo weaponize energy supplies, quadrupling crude oil prices and forcing Western European democracies and Japan to shift their foreign policy away from unconditional support for Israel?

  2. [02:45] Explain: Explain how Vietcong guerrilla tactics—including subterranean tunnel systems, booby traps, and ambushes—neutralized superior American aerial firepower and chemical defoliants.
  3. [04:20] Challenge: Evaluate why the January 1968 Tet Offensive was simultaneously a crushing tactical defeat for communist forces, yet a decisive strategic and political victory that ended the US war effort.

lessonTitle: Proxy Wars: Why did the superpowers fight in Asia (Korea & Vietnam)?
title: The Unbearable Lightness of Being (1988, Philip Kaufman) | Original Trailer
teacher_guidance: Acclaimed feature film adaptation of Milan Kundera’s novel starring Daniel Day-Lewis and Juliette Binoche, depicting the intoxicating artistic and intellectual freedom of the 1968 Prague Spring, shattered by the thunder of Soviet tanks rolling into Prague in August 1968. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–02:26 (Full Trailer). Lesson Phase: Cinematic Starter Hook & The Crushing of the Prague Spring. Tone Alert: Passionate, evocative historical drama blending romance and political invasion.
viewing_task: Cinematic Discussion Focus: Notice the joyful intellectual, cultural, and sexual awakening of Prague in early 1968 ("Socialism with a Human Face"), followed by the violent arrival of Soviet Warsaw Pact tanks, camera lenses documenting the protests, and the crushing of civilian freedom. How does the film illustrate the profound emotional shock experienced by Czech citizens when their reformist dream was brutally extinguished by Soviet forces?

lessonTitle: Proxy Wars: Why did the superpowers fight in Asia (Korea & Vietnam)?
title: CNN Cold War Episode 14: Red Spring (1968) | Jeremy Isaacs Production
teacher_guidance: Landmark documentary chronicling Alexander Dubček’s Action Programme ("Socialism with a Human Face"), the abolition of censorship, Soviet anxieties over the "domino effect" in Poland and East Germany, Operation Danube (500,000 Warsaw Pact troops invading Czechoslovakia), and the formulation of the Brezhnev Doctrine. Recommended Watch Window: 18:30–31:00 • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Ideological Heterodoxy. Tone Alert: Exceptional documentary featuring interviews with Alexander Dubček, Czech student protesters, and Soviet military commanders.
viewing_task:
1. [07:40] Recall: What famous phrase did Alexander Dubček use to describe his vision of reformed, democratic communism in Czechoslovakia during the 1968 Prague Spring?
  2. [22:15] Explain: Explain why Leonid Brezhnev and other Warsaw Pact leaders (like East Germany's Walter Ulbricht) feared that Czech freedom of speech and press would destroy the entire Soviet bloc.
  3. [35:40] Challenge: Evaluate the ideological significance of the Brezhnev Doctrine issued in November 1968: how did it redefine the sovereignty of Eastern European nations and justify military aggression within the socialist camp?

lessonTitle: Fall of the Berlin Wall (1989) and the collapse of the Soviet Union (1991).
title: The Rise and Fall of the Berlin Wall | TED-Ed
teacher_guidance: Konrad H. Jarausch explores the construction of the Berlin Wall in August 1961 to stem the brain drain of 2.7 million East Germans, and its dramatic opening on 9 November 1989. Recommended Watch Window: 00:30–04:45 • Lesson Phase: Quick Starter Check (0–3m). Tone Alert: Fast, accessible animated educational summary of Cold War division and popular uprising.
viewing_task:
1. [01:10] Quick Check: Why did East German leader Walter Ulbricht and Nikita Khrushchev order the construction of the Berlin Wall in August 1961?
  2. [03:40] Hinge Question: How did Günter Schabowski's botched live press conference on the evening of 9 November 1989 accidentally trigger the immediate, euphoric fall of the Berlin Wall?

lessonTitle: Fall of the Berlin Wall (1989) and the collapse of the Soviet Union (1991).
title: Perestroika & Glasnost (The End of the Soviet Union) | Simple History
teacher_guidance: Analyzes Mikhail Gorbachev’s twin policies of Glasnost (political openness) and Perestroika (economic restructuring), the renunciation of the Brezhnev Doctrine, and the dissolution of the USSR on 25 December 1991. Recommended Watch Window: 01:00–06:45 • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Archival Investigation. Tone Alert: Clear, structured animated overview of Soviet political and economic collapse.
viewing_task:
1. [02:10] Recall: Define the Russian terms Glasnost and Perestroika introduced by General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev after coming to power in 1985.
  2. [04:30] Explain: Explain how Gorbachev's decision to abandon the Brezhnev Doctrine (the "Sinatra Doctrine") led directly to the peaceful overthrow of communist dictatorships across Eastern Europe in 1989.
  3. [06:15] Challenge: Evaluate why Gorbachev's attempts to save the Soviet Union ended in its total dissolution: did economic failure or ethnic nationalism destroy the USSR?

lessonTitle: Fall of the Berlin Wall (1989) and the collapse of the Soviet Union (1991).
title: Charlie Wilson's War (2007, Mike Nichols / Tom Hanks) | Official Trailer
teacher_guidance: Sharp, witty Hollywood dramatisation of Texas Congressman Charlie Wilson, CIA operative Gust Avrakotos, and socialite Joanne Herring orchestrating Operation Cyclone: covertly funneling billions of dollars in Stinger surface-to-air missiles to Afghan Mujahideen fighting the Soviet Red Army. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–02:31 (Full Trailer). Lesson Phase: Cinematic Starter Hook & Covert Proxy Warfare. Tone Alert: Engaging geopolitical drama with an incisive look at covert Cold War operations.
viewing_task: Cinematic Discussion Focus: Notice the backroom Washington political deals, the sophisticated CIA weapons supply routes through Pakistan and Israel, and how shoulder-fired Stinger anti-aircraft missiles revolutionized the war in Afghanistan by destroying Soviet Mi-24 Hind attack helicopters. How does the film capture the unintended long-term consequences of superpower proxy warfare?

lessonTitle: Fall of the Berlin Wall (1989) and the collapse of the Soviet Union (1991).
title: CNN Cold War Episode 20: Soldiers of God (1977–1988) | Jeremy Isaacs Production
teacher_guidance: Comprehensive documentary detailing the December 1979 Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, the rise of the Mujahideen insurgency, the US boycott of the 1980 Moscow Olympics, President Carter's cancellation of grain sales, and the ten-year quagmire that bled the Soviet military of morale and treasure. Recommended Watch Window: 12:30–25:00 • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & The Afghan Trap. Tone Alert: Sobering military and diplomatic documentary featuring interviews with Zbigniew Brzezinski, Soviet veterans, and Mujahideen commanders.
viewing_task:
1. [06:30] Recall: In what month and year did the Soviet Red Army invade Afghanistan to prop up the embattled Marxist government in Kabul?
  2. [18:15] Explain: How did President Jimmy Carter respond diplomatically and economically to the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, effectively bringing the era of Détente to an abrupt end?
  3. [31:40] Challenge: Evaluate why Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev later described the Soviet-Afghan War as a "bleeding wound": how did the conflict contribute to the internal collapse of the USSR?

lessonTitle: Assessment: Was the Cold War ever truly 'cold'?
title: Cold War Files: The Conflicts That Turned the Cold War Hot | Dark Archives
teacher_guidance: Anchors the synoptic assessment debate: while Europe remained an "armed peace" without direct superpower combat, over 20 million people died in proxy wars across the Global South. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–03:45 • Lesson Phase: Quick Starter Check (0–3m). Tone Alert: Fast, analytical documentary examining the global human cost of superpower rivalry.
viewing_task:
1. [00:50] Quick Check: Why do many global historians argue that calling the conflict the "Cold War" is inaccurate and Eurocentric?
  2. [02:30] Hinge Question: How did superpower rivalry in nations like Angola, Mozambique, Nicaragua, and Afghanistan transform local civil conflicts into devastating proxy battlefields?

lessonTitle: Assessment: Was the Cold War ever truly 'cold'?
title: When Did the Cold War Actually Start? | History Matters
teacher_guidance: Historiographical capstone analyzing the three major schools of thought on Cold War origins: 1917 (Bolshevik Revolution), 1945 (Yalta/Potsdam/Hiroshima), or 1947 (Truman Doctrine/Marshall Plan). Recommended Watch Window: 01:00–07:15 • Lesson Phase: Capstone Synoptic Synthesis & Historiographical Evaluation. Tone Alert: Insightful, academically rigorous historiographical review of Cold War scholarship.
viewing_task:
1. [02:15] Recall: Identify the three major competing dates proposed by historians for the outbreak of the Cold War (1917, 1945, 1947).
  2. [04:30] Explain: Explain the Orthodox (traditionalist) vs. Revisionist historical debate regarding who bears primary responsibility for starting the Cold War.
  3. [06:45] Challenge: Post-Revisionist Historiography: Assess John Lewis Gaddis' conclusion that the Cold War was caused by mutual misperception, geopolitical insecurity, and the inevitable clash of two empires rather than one-sided aggression.

lessonTitle: Assessment: Was the Cold War ever truly 'cold'?

teacher_guidance: Academy Award-winning masterpiece portraying Stasi Captain Gerd Wiesler conducting round-the-clock audio surveillance on an East Berlin playwright in 1984, capturing the suffocating paranoia, informers, and police state control before the fall of the Wall. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–02:18 (Full Trailer). Lesson Phase: Cinematic Starter Hook & The Reality of the Stasi Surveillance State. Tone Alert: Tense, emotionally profound German psychological thriller.
viewing_task: Cinematic Discussion Focus: Notice the tape recorders, wiretapped apartments, secret index cards, and pervasive fear of betrayal depicted in this Oscar-winning film about East Germany's Stasi. How does the trailer demonstrate the human cost of totalitarian surveillance, and why did millions of citizens rejoice when the Berlin Wall and the communist police state collapsed in November 1989?

lessonTitle: Assessment: Was the Cold War ever truly 'cold'?

teacher_guidance: Dramatic documentary covering the miraculous events of 1989: the Polish Round Table talks, the opening of Hungary's Austrian border, the peaceful mass demonstrations in Leipzig, the collapse of the Berlin Wall on 9 November, and the Velvet Revolution in Prague. Recommended Watch Window: 26:00–38:00 • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & The Miracle of 1989. Tone Alert: Euphoric, historically monumental documentary featuring Mikhail Gorbachev, George H.W. Bush, Helmut Kohl, and ordinary Berliners at Checkpoint Charlie.
viewing_task:
1. [11:20] Recall: In which Eastern European country did the trade union movement Solidarity (Solidarność), led by Lech Wałęsa, force free elections in June 1989, forming the first non-communist government in the Eastern bloc?
  2. [24:10] Explain: How did Hungary’s decision to dismantle its electrified barbed-wire border with neutral Austria in May 1989 create a massive breach in the Iron Curtain for East German refugees?
  3. [36:45] Challenge: Evaluate the personal leadership and chemistry between Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev (from Geneva 1985 to Reykjavik 1986 and the 1987 INF Treaty): was the peaceful end of the Cold War driven by Western military pressure or Soviet internal reform?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 3: The Anglo-German Naval Arms Race & HMS Dreadnought (1898–1914)

lessonTitle: Enquiry 3: The Anglo-German Naval Arms Race & HMS Dreadnought (1898–1914)

lessonTitle: Enquiry 3: The Anglo-German Naval Arms Race & HMS Dreadnought (1898–1914)

lessonTitle: Enquiry 4: The Alliance Systems & the Balkan Powder Keg (1879–1913)

  3. [05:20] Challenge: Analyze the dilemma facing the Austro-Hungarian Dual Monarchy: why did Vienna fear that growing South Slav nationalism inside its empire would lead to total imperial dismemberment?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 4: The Alliance Systems & the Balkan Powder Keg (1879–1913)

  3. [06:45] Challenge: Evaluate the role of the press and public opinion in 1914: did bellicose newspaper headlines force politicians into aggressive stances?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 5: The July Crisis: Sarajevo to the Outbreak of War (June–August 1914)

How does this film capture the tragic chasm between romantic pre-war propaganda and the brutal reality of industrialised warfare?

lessonTitle: November Assessment Masterclass: Why Did War Break Out in 1914?

lessonTitle: Why were young men so desperate to join the slaughter of 1914?

viewing_task:

  3. [02:30] Challenge: Evaluate the impact of the first day of the Battle of the Somme (1 July 1916) on towns like Accrington: why did the British Army never form Pals Battalions again?

lessonTitle: Why were young men so desperate to join the slaughter of 1914?

viewing_task: Cinematic Discussion Focus: Notice how British cavalry officers eagerly charge across open fields with drawn sabres, only to be cut down by concealed German machine-gun nests and wire. How does Spielberg dramatize the catastrophic obsolescence of traditional military tactics in the face of modern industrial weaponry?

lessonTitle: Why were young men so desperate to join the slaughter of 1914?

lessonTitle: Did British generals make the horror of trench warfare worse?

lessonTitle: Did British generals make the horror of trench warfare worse?

lessonTitle: Did British generals make the horror of trench warfare worse?

lessonTitle: The Reformation & The Break with Rome (1517–1547)

viewing_task:

  3. [04:30] Challenge: Evaluate whether Henry VIII was a true Protestant theological reformer or merely a self-interested Catholic monarch without a Pope.

lessonTitle: The Reformation & The Break with Rome (1517–1547)

Lesson Phase: Cinematic Starter Hook & Conscience vs Tyranny. Tone Alert: Tense, intellectually profound Tudor drama.
viewing_task: Cinematic Discussion Focus: Notice Paul Scofield's portrayal of Sir Thomas More refusing to sign Henry VIII's oath, declaring: "Some men think the Earth is round, others think it flat; but if it is flat, could the King's command make it round?" How does this cinematic sequence dramatize the terrifying clash between absolute royal authority and individual moral conscience during the Tudor Reformation?

lessonTitle: The Reformation & The Break with Rome (1517–1547)

viewing_task:

  2. [18:40] Explain: Explain how the fall of Cardinal Thomas Wolsey in 1529 demonstrated the perilous danger of failing to deliver Henry VIII's marital annulment.
  3. [24:15] Challenge: Evaluate how the execution of Bishop John Fisher and Sir Thomas More in 1535 shocked Christian Europe and permanently branded Henry as a bloodthirsty tyrant.

lessonTitle: Elizabeth I & The Middle Way (1558–1588)

lessonTitle: Elizabeth I & The Middle Way (1558–1588)

  3. [18:40] Challenge: Capstone Evaluation: Assess whether the English Bill of Rights truly established a democracy in 1689, or merely replaced the absolute rule of a King with the oligarchy of wealthy landowners and aristocrats.

title: What Was the 'Scramble for Africa'? | BBC What's New
teacher_guidance: Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–03:00 | Lesson Phase: Lesson Hook | Tone Alert: Concise introduction to the 1884–85 Berlin Conference and colonial partition.
viewing_task:
[00:55] Quick Check: What percentage of Africa was under European control in 1870 compared to 1914?
[02:15] Hinge Question: Why were zero African leaders invited to the 1884 Berlin Conference where their continent was carved up?

lessonTitle: Why did European powers scramble for Africa, and how was empire justified?
title: The Scramble for Africa | Timelines.tv
teacher_guidance: Recommended Watch Window: 00:20–04:40 | Lesson Phase: Causal Breakdown | Tone Alert: Rigorous analysis of technological catalysts (Maxim gun, quinine, steamships) and raw material extraction.
viewing_task:
[01:10] Recall: What three technological breakthroughs enabled Europeans to penetrate the African interior in the late 19th century?
[02:30] Explain: How did industrial capitalism drive the search for raw materials (rubber, copper, palm oil, cotton) and captive consumer markets?
[04:00] Challenge: How did imperial ideologies like 'The Civilising Mission' and Social Darwinism serve to justify ruthless plunder?

lessonTitle: Why did European powers scramble for Africa, and how was empire justified?
title: Zulu (1964) | Original Movie Trailer (Michael Caine / Stanley Baker)
teacher_guidance: Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–02:24 | Lesson Phase: Visual & Cultural Impact | Tone Alert: Classic cinema depicting the 1879 Battle of Rorke's Drift during the Anglo-Zulu War.
viewing_task: [01:15] Cinematic Discussion Focus: How does the film frame British imperial soldiers facing the Zulu impi? How does cinema shape public memory of imperial military conflicts?

lessonTitle: Why did European powers scramble for Africa, and how was empire justified?
title: Empire: Scramble for Africa & Imperial Ideology | BBC / Jeremy Paxman
teacher_guidance: Recommended Watch Window: 18:00–42:00 | Lesson Phase: Flipped Learning / Extension | Tone Alert: Investigates Cecil Rhodes, the British South Africa Company, and Victorian racial theories.
viewing_task:
[20:30] Recall: What was Cecil Rhodes' vision of a 'Cape to Cairo' railway?
[30:00] Explain: How did private chartered companies like the British South Africa Company conquer territory ahead of formal government annexation?
[39:45] Challenge: How did the arbitrary borders drawn by European diplomats in 1885 create enduring ethnic and political conflict across modern Africa?

lessonTitle: Who truly benefited from the British Empire?
title: Was the British Empire a Force for Good? (Part 1) | BBC Bitesize
teacher_guidance: Recommended Watch Window: 00:20–05:30 | Lesson Phase: Historiographical Debate | Tone Alert: Balanced debate exploring infrastructure, railways, and legal codes vs exploitation and famine.
viewing_task:
[01:30] Quick Check: What infrastructure did the British construct in India, and who primarily paid for it?
[04:45] Hinge Question: Were imperial railways built primarily to benefit the Indian public or to transport British troops and extract raw materials to ports?

lessonTitle: Who truly benefited from the British Empire?
title: Was the British Empire a Force for Good? (Part 2) | BBC Bitesize
teacher_guidance: Recommended Watch Window: 00:30–06:30 | Lesson Phase: Deep Historiographical Synthesis | Tone Alert: Evaluates the human cost, deindustrialisation of native economies, and unequal power dynamics.
viewing_task:
[01:45] Recall: How did British tariffs destroy the traditional Indian handloom textile industry?
[03:50] Explain: What role did free-market dogma play in British government inaction during imperial famines in India and Ireland?
[05:40] Challenge: In evaluating whether the empire was a 'force for good', why must historians examine whose voices and perspectives are being prioritized?

lessonTitle: Who truly benefited from the British Empire?
title: Gandhi (1982) | Official Movie Trailer (Ben Kingsley / Richard Attenborough)
teacher_guidance: Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–02:56 | Lesson Phase: Visual & Cultural Impact | Tone Alert: Multi-Oscar-winning historical epic depicting satyagraha and the dismantling of the British Raj.
viewing_task: [01:40] Cinematic Discussion Focus: How does the film frame Mahatma Gandhi's strategy of non-violent civil disobedience against the military might of the British Empire?

lessonTitle: Who truly benefited from the British Empire?
title: The Legacy of the British Empire | Historical Analysis & Evidence
teacher_guidance: Recommended Watch Window: 15:00–38:00 | Lesson Phase: Synoptic Review | Tone Alert: Deep critical assessment of the economic, cultural, and political legacy of the British Empire.
viewing_task:
[18:30] Recall: What was the 'drain of wealth' theory articulated by Indian nationalists like Dadabhai Naoroji?
[28:00] Explain: How did the British divide-and-rule strategy exacerbate religious divisions that led to the bloody Partition of India in 1947?
[36:00] Challenge: How does the legacy of the British Empire continue to shape modern British society, multiculturalism, and global economics?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 1: Who were the Jews of Europe before the Second World War?
title: What is the Holocaust? Part 1/7: Introduction | Yad Vashem
teacher_guidance: Concise introductory overview from Yad Vashem defining the Holocaust as the state-sponsored, systematic persecution and murder of six million Jews by the Nazi regime and its collaborators. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–00:55 (Full Clip) • Lesson Phase: Quick Starter Check (0–3m). Tone Alert: Solemn, dignified educational overview.
viewing_task:
1. [00:20] Quick Check: Approximately how many European Jewish men, women, and children were systematically murdered by Nazi Germany and its collaborators during the Holocaust?
  2. [00:45] Hinge Question: Why is it historically essential to understand who European Jews were and how they lived before 1939, rather than viewing them solely as passive victims of Nazi violence?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 1: Who were the Jews of Europe before the Second World War?
title: Jewish Life before the Second World War: an Introduction | Yad Vashem
teacher_guidance: Yad Vashem’s foundational documentary exploring the vibrant diversity of European Jewish life before 1939: religious, secular, Yiddish culture in the shtetls of Poland, and urban integration in Berlin, Vienna, and Paris. Recommended Watch Window: 00:30–04:45 • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Historical Grounding. Tone Alert: Solemn, dignified educational documentary honoring pre-war Jewish culture and human dignity.
viewing_task:
1. [01:10] Recall: Approximately how many Jewish people lived in Europe prior to the Second World War in 1939, and in which country was the largest Jewish population concentrated?
  2. [02:40] Explain: Contrast the lifestyle of Jews living in the rural shtetls of Eastern Europe with that of integrated, secular Jewish communities in Western European capitals like Berlin, Vienna, and Paris.
  3. [04:15] Challenge: Why is it historically essential to study pre-war Jewish life, culture, and achievements before studying the Holocaust: why must victims not be defined solely by their destruction?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 1: Who were the Jews of Europe before the Second World War?
title: Life is Beautiful (1997, Roberto Benigni) | Official Trailer
teacher_guidance: Three-time Academy Award-winning film portraying Guido Orefice, a playful Italian-Jewish bookshop owner whose life is shattered by fascist racial laws and deportation. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–02:14 (Full Trailer). Lesson Phase: Cinematic Starter Hook & Family Life. Tone Alert: Poignant, imaginative dramatisation of pre-war affection and family solidarity.
viewing_task: Cinematic Discussion Focus: Notice how Roberto Benigni depicts the vibrancy, humour, and romantic daily life of Guido and Dora in 1930s Italy before the implementation of racial laws and deportation. How does this cinematic framing emphasize that Holocaust victims were ordinary individuals with rich emotional lives, professions, and families?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 1: Who were the Jews of Europe before the Second World War?
title: Liberators and Survivors: The First Moments | Yad Vashem
teacher_guidance: Moving oral history documentary featuring firsthand testimonies from survivors recalling their childhood homes, schools, and Sabbath traditions before the cataclysm. Recommended Watch Window: 01:00–08:30 • Lesson Phase: In-Depth Documentary Investigation & Survivor Testimony. Tone Alert: Dignified, moving survivor memories honoring lost communities.
viewing_task:
1. [02:15] Recall: What languages and cultural traditions were spoken and practiced by Eastern European Jewish families in pre-war Poland and Lithuania?
  2. [05:40] Explain: How do survivor recollections illustrate the sudden transformation of daily life when anti-Semitic laws and social ostracism began separating Jewish children from their classmates?
  3. [07:50] Challenge: Evaluate how oral testimonies restore personal individuality and human dignity to individuals who were reduced to numbers tattooed on their arms.

lessonTitle: Enquiry 2: How were German Jews progressively stripped of citizenship and rights (1933–1939)?
title: What Was Kristallnacht in the Holocaust? | Holocaust Explainer
teacher_guidance: Concise explainer detailing the 9–10 November 1938 nationwide pogrom: the destruction of synagogues, looting of businesses, and mass arrest of 30,000 men. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–03:00 • Lesson Phase: Quick Starter Check (0–3m). Tone Alert: Clear, focused museum breakdown of state-sponsored terror.
viewing_task:
1. [01:00] Quick Check: What pretext did Propaganda Minister Joseph Goebbels use to launch the violent nationwide pogrom known as Kristallnacht in November 1938?
  2. [02:15] Hinge Question: Why did the arrest and incarceration of 30,000 Jewish men in concentration camps during Kristallnacht signal that legal emigration was no longer enough to escape persecution?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 2: How were German Jews progressively stripped of citizenship and rights (1933–1939)?
title: The Path to Nazi Genocide: From Citizens to Outcasts, 1933–1938 | USHMM
teacher_guidance: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM) chapter tracing the legal and social exclusion of German Jews: the April 1933 boycott, the 1935 Nuremberg Laws (Reich Citizenship Law and Blood Protection Law), and the November 1938 Kristallnacht pogrom. Recommended Watch Window: 01:00–06:15 • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Legal Deconstruction. Tone Alert: Authoritative museum documentary with primary Nazi legislation and photographs.
viewing_task:
1. [01:45] Recall: What two foundational statutes comprised the September 1935 Nuremberg Laws passed by the Nazi Reichstag at the Nuremberg Party Rally?
  2. [03:30] Explain: Explain how the Reich Citizenship Law stripped German Jews of their constitutional citizenship, reducing them to second-class "subjects of the state" (Staatsangehörige).
  3. [05:20] Challenge: Evaluate how the state-orchestrated violence of Kristallnacht (9–10 November 1938) marked a decisive transition from discriminatory civil legislation to violent physical terror and mass roundups.

lessonTitle: Enquiry 2: How were German Jews progressively stripped of citizenship and rights (1933–1939)?
title: Schindler's List (1993, Steven Spielberg) | Official Trailer
teacher_guidance: Seven-time Academy Award-winning historical masterpiece starring Liam Neeson, Ralph Fiennes, and Ben Kingsley. Depicts the progressive stripping of Jewish rights, forced relocation into enclosed ghettos, and the liquidation of communities. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–02:15 (Full Trailer). Lesson Phase: Cinematic Starter Hook & Legal Dispossession. Tone Alert: Severe, historically unflinching cinematic drama in monochrome.
viewing_task: Cinematic Discussion Focus: Notice the stark black-and-white cinematography, the red coat of the little girl, the systematic eviction of families from their apartments, and the methodical bureaucratic documentation of confiscated Jewish property. How does Spielberg's visual choices illustrate the ruthless dehumanisation of an entire people under Nazi rule?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 2: How were German Jews progressively stripped of citizenship and rights (1933–1939)?
title: What Were the Nuremberg Trials? | Holocaust Explainer | USHMM
teacher_guidance: Detailed analysis of how Nazi legal architects like Wilhelm Frick and Hans Frank were held accountable under international law for "Crimes Against Humanity", establishing that state laws cannot excuse genocidal atrocities. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–04:00 (Full Explainer). Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Legal Culpability. Tone Alert: Rigorous legal-historical documentary from the US Holocaust Memorial Museum.
viewing_task:
1. [00:50] Recall: What new legal concept was formulated at the 1945–1946 Nuremberg International Military Tribunal to prosecute state-sponsored persecution and genocide?
  2. [02:15] Explain: How did Nazi defendants attempt to defend their implementation of the Nuremberg Laws and anti-Semitic decrees, and why did the tribunal reject their "superior orders" defense?
  3. [03:30] Challenge: Evaluate the enduring legacy of the Nuremberg Principles: how did the trials establish that individual human conscience supersedes the obedience demanded by totalitarian state laws?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 3: How did the outbreak of WWII transform Nazi anti-Jewish policy (1939–1941)?
title: The Warsaw Ghetto Uprising | Key Historical Concepts | Yad Vashem
teacher_guidance: Concise Yad Vashem overview of the Jewish Combat Organisation (ŻOB), Mordechai Anielewicz, and the April 1943 armed uprising in the Warsaw Ghetto against German deportation forces. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–03:20 • Lesson Phase: Quick Starter Check (0–3m). Tone Alert: Fast, stirring historical summary of armed defiance.
viewing_task:
1. [00:45] Quick Check: Who was the 24-year-old leader of the Jewish Combat Organisation (ŻOB) who commanded the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising in April 1943?
  2. [02:10] Hinge Question: Why did the young fighters of the Warsaw Ghetto choose to stage an armed uprising knowing that military defeat was inevitable?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 3: How did the outbreak of WWII transform Nazi anti-Jewish policy (1939–1941)?
title: What Were Ghettos in the Holocaust? | USHMM Explainer
teacher_guidance: USHMM explainer analyzing the establishment of over 1,000 enclosed ghettos across occupied Poland and the Baltic states: overcrowding, Star of David armbands, the Jewish Councils (Judenräte), starvation rations, and typhus epidemics. Recommended Watch Window: 00:30–03:50 • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Primary Analysis. Tone Alert: Objective, somber museum history detailing human suffering and social isolation.
viewing_task:
1. [01:05] Recall: What was the largest enclosed ghetto in Nazi-occupied Europe, where over 400,000 Jews were crammed into an area of barely 1.3 square miles surrounded by 10-foot brick walls?
  2. [02:15] Explain: How did Nazi occupation authorities use deliberate starvation rations (giving Jews barely 200 calories per day) and sanitary deprivation to weaponize disease and hunger inside the ghettos?
  3. [03:10] Challenge: Evaluate the agonizing moral dilemmas forced upon the Jewish Councils (Judenräte) appointed by the SS: did cooperation help protect communities or make leaders unwitting instruments of Nazi deportation?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 3: How did the outbreak of WWII transform Nazi anti-Jewish policy (1939–1941)?
title: The Pianist (2002, Roman Polanski / Adrien Brody) | Official Trailer
teacher_guidance: Three-time Academy Award-winning feature film based on the autobiography of Polish-Jewish classical pianist Władysław Szpilman, directed by Holocaust survivor Roman Polanski. Depicts the construction of the Warsaw Ghetto brick wall, the smuggling of food by children, and the deportations to Treblinka. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–02:16 (Full Trailer). Lesson Phase: Cinematic Starter Hook & Ghetto Survival. Tone Alert: Intense, visceral biographical drama.
viewing_task: Cinematic Discussion Focus: Notice the physical bricking up of the Warsaw Ghetto walls, the starving children begging in the streets, the arbitrary violence of SS officers, and Władysław Szpilman's struggle to maintain his musical identity amidst total devastation. How does Polanski portray the gradual, agonizing erosion of human dignity inside the enclosed ghetto?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 3: How did the outbreak of WWII transform Nazi anti-Jewish policy (1939–1941)?
title: The Great Deportation in the Warsaw Ghetto - Abraham Lewin's Diary | Yad Vashem
teacher_guidance: Haunting primary archival documentary examining the secret Oneg Shabbat underground archive compiled by historian Emanuel Ringelblum, buried in metal milk cans beneath the ghetto rubble. Recommended Watch Window: 01:00–07:15 • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Primary Document Investigation. Tone Alert: Devastating primary diary excerpts read against historical photographs.
viewing_task:
1. [01:40] Recall: What was the codename of the secret underground archive established by Emanuel Ringelblum to document daily life and Nazi atrocities in the Warsaw Ghetto?
  2. [03:50] Explain: Describe Abraham Lewin's diary entries recording the "Great Deportation" (Grossaktion Warschau) in the summer of 1942: how many Jews were loaded into cattle cars destined for Treblinka death camp each day?
  3. [06:30] Challenge: Evaluate the profound moral significance of the Oneg Shabbat archive: why did Ringelblum and his colleagues risk their lives to bury their writings in milk cans beneath the earth?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 4: How and why did persecution turn into systematic mass murder (1941–1942)?
title: Einsatzgruppen: Mobile Killing Squads | USHMM
teacher_guidance: Analyzes the invasion of the Soviet Union (Operation Barbarossa, June 1941) and the transition to systematic mass murder: Einsatzgruppen A, B, C, D, Order Police Battalions, local collaborators, and the massacre at Babi Yar. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–04:00 • Lesson Phase: Quick Starter Check (0–3m). Tone Alert: Highly sensitive, serious archival documentary detailing the "Holocaust by Bullets".
viewing_task:
1. [01:15] Quick Check: What were the four mobile paramilitary death squads created by the SS to execute Jews behind the Eastern Front in 1941 called?
  2. [03:10] Hinge Question: Why did SS commanders like Heinrich Himmler conclude that mass shootings by firing squad were inefficient and psychologically unviable for executioners, driving the development of industrial gas chambers?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 4: How and why did persecution turn into systematic mass murder (1941–1942)?
title: Holocaust by Bullets - Father Patrick Desbois | Yahad-In Unum Lecture
teacher_guidance: Groundbreaking forensic investigation by French Catholic priest Father Patrick Desbois, documenting the mass execution trenches of over two million Jews across Ukraine, Belarus, Poland, and Russia through ballistics and local eyewitness interviews. Recommended Watch Window: 04:00–12:30 • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Forensic Grounding. Tone Alert: Emotionally solemn, highly rigorous forensic history.
viewing_task:
1. [06:15] Recall: How many Jewish victims are estimated to have been murdered by bullets rather than in extermination camps, and across which territories did these killings occur?
  2. [10:30] Explain: Describe Father Desbois' methodology: how does his team use German military archives, Soviet extraordinary commissions, GPS mapping, and local non-Jewish eyewitness interviews to locate mass graves?
  3. [12:15] Challenge: Evaluate how the reality of the "Holocaust by Bullets" destroys the myth that the genocide was carried out in secret camps far from public view.

lessonTitle: Enquiry 4: How and why did persecution turn into systematic mass murder (1941–1942)?
title: Conspiracy (2001, Frank Pierson / Kenneth Branagh) | Original Trailer
teacher_guidance: Acclaimed HBO/BBC film starring Kenneth Branagh as Reinhard Heydrich and Colin Firth as Wilhelm Stuckart, dramatizing the 90-minute Wannsee Conference on 20 January 1942 where 15 high-ranking Nazi bureaucrats formalized the "Final Solution". Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–01:01 (Full Trailer). Lesson Phase: Cinematic Starter Hook & The Bureaucracy of Genocide. Tone Alert: Chilling, polished depiction of civil servants organizing industrial extermination over lunch.
viewing_task: Cinematic Discussion Focus: Notice the opulent lakeside villa, the polite administrative decorum, fine wine, and crisp bureaucratic language ("evacuation to the East", "cleansing") used by SS General Reinhard Heydrich and ministry officials. How does this film capture the terrifying banality of evil: how educated lawyers, economists, and civil servants became architects of mass murder?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 4: How and why did persecution turn into systematic mass murder (1941–1942)?
title: Auschwitz: The Nazis and the Final Solution | BBC Select
teacher_guidance: Laurence Rees' acclaimed BBC documentary series examining the architectural and bureaucratic evolution of mass murder from gas vans to Zyklon B chambers. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–03:07 (Full Clip) • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Historical Evolution. Tone Alert: Rigorous, authoritative BBC documentary with rare archival footage.
viewing_task:
1. [00:45] Recall: In what Berlin suburb was the secret 1942 conference held where the logistical execution of the "Final Solution" was coordinated across German state ministries?
  2. [01:45] Explain: Explain how the transition from mobile Einsatzgruppen shootings to fixed extermination camps was designed to accelerate the pace of murder while shielding German executioners from psychological breakdown.
  3. [02:30] Challenge: Evaluate how the railway logistics of the German Reichsbahn made the continent-wide deportation of millions of people possible during an active two-front war.

lessonTitle: Enquiry 5: How did the "Final Solution" operate, and how did Jews resist?
title: What Was Auschwitz? | USHMM Explainer
teacher_guidance: USHMM explainer analyzing the Auschwitz-Birkenau complex: the distinction between labor camps and extermination centers, the selection ramp (die Rampe), Zyklon B gas chambers, and the October 1944 Sonderkommando uprising. Recommended Watch Window: 00:20–03:25 • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Structural Analysis. Tone Alert: Serious museum explainer analyzing industrial extermination and armed resistance.
viewing_task:
1. [00:45] Quick Check: What were the three main constituent parts of the Auschwitz camp complex in occupied Poland (Auschwitz I, Auschwitz II-Birkenau, Auschwitz III-Monowitz)?
  2. [01:45] Hinge Question: How did SS doctors make the split-second life-or-death decisions on the selection ramp at Birkenau, and what proportion of arriving prisoners were murdered immediately?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 5: How did the "Final Solution" operate, and how did Jews resist?
title: The Auschwitz Album: Visual Evidence Leading to Mass Murder | Yad Vashem
teacher_guidance: Visual examination of the unique photographic album discovered by survivor Lili Jacob, documenting the arrival and selection of Hungarian Jews on the Birkenau ramp in May 1944. Recommended Watch Window: 00:45–05:15 • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Visual Forensic Analysis. Tone Alert: Solemn, forensic documentary examining primary photographic evidence.
viewing_task:
1. [01:10] Recall: Who took the photographs contained in the "Auschwitz Album", and why were these images originally captured?
  2. [03:20] Explain: Explain what the photographs reveal about the deliberate Nazi deception tactics used to keep arriving victims calm as they walked toward Crematoria II and III.
  3. [04:45] Challenge: Why is the Auschwitz Album considered one of the most critical visual records of the Holocaust: how does it provide incontrovertible photographic proof of industrial genocide?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 5: How did the "Final Solution" operate, and how did Jews resist?
title: Son of Saul (2015, László Nemes) | Official Trailer
teacher_guidance: Academy Award and Cannes Grand Prix-winning masterpiece following Saul Ausländer, a Hungarian Jewish member of the Auschwitz-Birkenau Sonderkommando forced to work in the crematoria, who risks everything to give a dead child a proper Jewish burial. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–01:50 (Full Trailer). Lesson Phase: Cinematic Starter Hook & Spiritual Defiance. Tone Alert: Intensely claustrophobic, uncompromising historical drama.
viewing_task: Cinematic Discussion Focus: Notice the shallow depth of field (the camera stays locked tightly on Saul's face while horrors remain blurred in the background), the immersive soundscape of metallic doors, shouts, and machinery, and Saul's obsessive quest to give a child a proper burial. How does director László Nemes use cinematic technique to convey both the physical inferno of Birkenau and an individual's desperate effort to preserve their humanity?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 5: How did the "Final Solution" operate, and how did Jews resist?
title: What Was the Liberation of Nazi Camps? | Holocaust Explainer | USHMM
teacher_guidance: Documents the arrival of Soviet, British, and American forces at Majdanek, Auschwitz, Buchenwald, and Dachau, contrasting initial soldier shock with the ongoing struggle to save dying survivors. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–03:04 (Full Explainer). Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & The Shock of Discovery. Tone Alert: Solemn archival footage from liberating cameramen.
viewing_task:
1. [00:45] Recall: Which army liberated the Auschwitz-Birkenau extermination camp on 27 January 1945, discovering barely 7,000 emaciated living prisoners?
  2. [01:30] Explain: What physical evidence of industrial murder did SS guards fail to destroy before fleeing the camp, including warehouses filled with personal belongings?
  3. [02:15] Challenge: Why did the date of the liberation of Auschwitz-Birkenau (27 January) become universally designated by the United Nations as International Holocaust Remembrance Day?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 6: Who was responsible, who collaborated, and who tried to save?
title: Who are the Righteous Among the Nations? | Yad Vashem
teacher_guidance: Animated explainer from Yad Vashem explaining the criteria for recognition as Righteous Among the Nations: non-Jewish individuals who risked their lives, freedom, or safety to save Jews during the Holocaust without monetary compensation. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–02:45 (Full Clip) • Lesson Phase: Quick Starter Check (0–3m). Tone Alert: Fast, accessible animated concept summary.
viewing_task:
1. [00:50] Quick Check: What three strict criteria does Yad Vashem require to bestow the honor of "Righteous Among the Nations"?
  2. [02:00] Hinge Question: Why did rescuing a Jewish family in occupied Eastern Europe require extraordinary moral and physical courage compared to Western Europe?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 6: Who was responsible, who collaborated, and who tried to save?
title: Why Almost All of Denmark's Jews Survived the Holocaust | Imperial War Museums
teacher_guidance: IWM curator documentary examining rescue and rescue networks: the Danish rescue of October 1943, where Danish fishermen ferried over 7,200 Jews to neutral Sweden in small boats, contrasting with complicity across occupied Europe. Recommended Watch Window: 01:00–06:45 • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Ethical Investigation. Tone Alert: Rigorous, uplifting museum documentary exploring moral responsibility and resistance.
viewing_task:
1. [01:45] Recall: What percentage of the Jewish population of Denmark survived the Holocaust as a result of the nationwide rescue operation in October 1943?
  2. [03:30] Explain: Explain how German naval attaché Georg Ferdinand Duckwitz leaked the planned Gestapo roundup, and how Danish doctors, police, clergy, and fishermen mobilized to hide and rescue their Jewish neighbors.
  3. [05:40] Challenge: Evaluate the spectrum of human behavior during the Shoah (perpetrators, collaborators, bystanders, and rescuers): why were rescuers like the Danish people or Raoul Wallenberg the rare exception rather than the rule?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 6: Who was responsible, who collaborated, and who tried to save?
title: One Life (2023, James Hawes / Anthony Hopkins) | Official Trailer
teacher_guidance: Acclaimed biographical drama starring Sir Anthony Hopkins and Johnny Flynn as Sir Nicholas Winton, who organized the Prague Kindertransport in 1939, rescuing 669 predominantly Jewish children from Nazi-occupied Czechoslovakia before borders closed. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–02:12 (Full Trailer). Lesson Phase: Cinematic Starter Hook & Moral Responsibility. Tone Alert: Deeply moving, uplifting historical drama exploring compassion and humility.
viewing_task: Cinematic Discussion Focus: Notice young Nicholas Winton racing against bureaucratic red tape and German troop movements in Prague, and decades later as an elderly man on the BBC television programme That's Life! surrounded by the adult children he saved. How does this film challenge the common historical excuse that "an ordinary individual was powerless to make a difference"?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 6: Who was responsible, who collaborated, and who tried to save?
title: Defiance (2008, Edward Zwick / Daniel Craig) | Official Trailer
teacher_guidance: Dramatisation of the Bielski partisans—brothers Tuvia, Zus, and Asael Bielski—who built a thriving hidden community of over 1,200 Jewish refugees in the Naliboki forest of Belarus, choosing armed resistance focused primarily on saving lives rather than military glory. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–02:27 (Full Trailer). Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Armed Jewish Resistance. Tone Alert: Tense, heroic historical combat drama highlighting active resistance.
viewing_task:
1. [00:45] Recall: In what densely forested region of Eastern Europe did the Bielski brothers establish an armed partisan community that successfully protected over 1,200 Jewish men, women, and children?
  2. [01:30] Explain: Contrast the philosophy of Tuvia Bielski ("I would rather save one old Jewish woman than kill ten German soldiers") with conventional military partisan resistance.
  3. [02:10] Challenge: How does the reality of the Bielski forest community shatter the persistent myth that Jewish victims passively accepted Nazi persecution without fighting back?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 7: What was lost, and what does survivor testimony teach us?
title: The Liberation of Bergen-Belsen Concentration Camp | Holocaust Memorial Day Trust
teacher_guidance: Archival newsreel of the British 11th Armoured Division liberating Bergen-Belsen on 15 April 1945, featuring Richard Dimbleby's historic BBC radio broadcast, medical relief, and survivor testimony. Recommended Watch Window: 00:00–02:35 • Lesson Phase: Quick Starter Check (0–3m). Tone Alert: Solemn, historical newsreel footage detailing the humanitarian catastrophe discovered by Allied forces.
viewing_task:
1. [00:40] Quick Check: Which Allied army liberated the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp in northern Germany on 15 April 1945, discovering 60,000 starving survivors and thousands of unburied corpses?
  2. [01:30] Hinge Question: Why did the BBC initially refuse to broadcast Richard Dimbleby's emotional dispatch from Bergen-Belsen until he threatened to resign?

lessonTitle: Enquiry 7: What was lost, and what does survivor testimony teach us?
title: What Was the Liberation of Nazi Camps? | Holocaust Explainer | USHMM
teacher_guidance: USHMM documentary detailing the liberation of camps across Europe, the medical disaster facing liberators, and the struggle of survivors who returned to find their entire families murdered. Recommended Watch Window: 00:30–03:00 • Lesson Phase: Guided Instruction & Post-Liberation Reality. Tone Alert: Sobering, respectful museum documentary.
viewing_task:
1. [00:45] Recall: What severe infectious disease was sweeping through Bergen-Belsen when British medical teams arrived, killing hundreds of survivors each day even after liberation?
  2. [01:40] Explain: Explain the immense difficulties faced by "Displaced Persons" (DPs) in post-war Europe: why could many survivors not return to their hometowns in Poland?
  3. [02:30] Challenge: Evaluate how the shock of camp liberations permanently altered Western public perceptions of Nazi Germany and shaped post-war human rights conventions.

lessonTitle: Enquiry 7: What was lost, and what does survivor testimony teach us?

[02:15] Recall: What symptoms characterized bubonic plague (painful buboes in armpits and groin) and pneumonic plague?

lessonTitle: To what extent did towns become filthier during the Early Modern period?

[03:45] Hinge Question: Why did it take nearly 250 years for Harington's flush toilet to be widely adopted across British homes?

lessonTitle: To what extent did towns become filthier during the Early Modern period?

viewing_task: [01:10] Cinematic Discussion Focus: How does the film contrast the debauched luxury of King Charles II's court with the filthy streets of London where the plague took hold?

lessonTitle: To what extent did towns become filthier during the Early Modern period?
title: The Great Plague (1665) | Timeline Documentary
